answer: Rule: the registry admits only 200 new identities per epoch, sold by sealed-bid auction. The clearing price is the exact per-identity cost, paid as stake that is burned if the identity is later proven a duplicate. An attacker buying 10 slots pays 10 times the clearing price, and their own bids push that price higher, so cost grows faster than linear. Like a garden with limited plots, growth is capped; the public atlas of identities makes duplicates visible, and the ivory ledger records every slot fee.
